summary: 快速眼动睡眠和脑成像研究为探讨梦的作用提供了依据，但关于梦的心理功能仍有不同解释。文章继而讨论梦与思考、解决问题及心理治疗的联系。
logic: 观察做梦时不同脑区的活动
讨论解题和治疗中的用途

paragraphs.brief: 在弗洛伊德之后，梦幻科学中最重要的事件是1950年代初期发现了一个睡眠阶段，其特点是脑活动强度大，眼睛运动迅速。
sentences: Thousands of years ago, dreams were seen as messages from the gods, and in many cultures, they are still considered prophetic, foretelling things to come.
几千年前，梦想被看成是神的讯息，在许多文化中，梦想仍被视为预言，预言未来的事情。
In ancient Greece, sick people slept at the temples of Asclepius, the god of medicine, in order to receive healing dreams.
在古希腊，病人睡在神的阿斯克莱皮乌斯的寺庙里，为了得到治愈的梦想。
Modern dream science really begins at the end of the 19th century with Sigmund Freud, who theorized that dreams were the expression of unconscious desires often from childhood.
现代的梦境科学真正始于19世纪末西格蒙德·弗洛伊德，他理论梦想是表达无意识的欲望从小。
He believed that exploring these hidden emotions through analysis could help cure mental illness.
他认为，通过分析探索这些隐藏的情绪有助于治疗精神病。
After Freud, the most important event in dream science was the discovery in the early 1950s of a phase of sleep characterized by intense brain activity and rapid eye movement (REM).
在弗洛伊德之后，梦幻科学中最重要的事件是1950年代初期发现了一个睡眠阶段，其特点是脑活动强度大，眼睛运动迅速。

paragraphs.brief: 成年人在REM里花大约四分之一的睡眠时间大部分时间是做梦
sentences: Adult humans spend about a quarter of their sleep time in REM, much of it dreaming.
成年人在REM里花大约四分之一的睡眠时间大部分时间是做梦
People awakened in the midst of REM sleep reported vivid dreams, which led researchers to conclude that most dreaming took place during REM.
人们在REM睡眠中醒来时，讲述了生动的梦想，研究人员因此得出结论，多数梦发生在REM。
Using a machine called the electroencephalograph (EEG), researchers were able to see that brain activity during REM resembled that of the brain when the body is awake.
研究人员使用一种叫做电脑图的机器，能够发现REM期间的大脑活动与身体清醒时的大脑活动相似。
The mystery of REM sleep is that even though it may not be essential, it is universal – at least in mammals and even birds.
REM睡眠的奥秘是，即使它可能不是必需的，但它是普遍的，至少在哺乳动物甚至鸟类中是如此。
Some researchers think REM may have evolved for physiological reasons.
一些研究人员认为REM可能已经进化了生理原因。
“One thing that’s unique about mammals and birds is that they regulate body temperature,” says neuroscientist Jerry Siegel, director of UCLA’s Center for Sleep Research.
说神经科学家杰里·西格尔加州大学洛杉矶分校睡眠研究中心的主任：“哺乳动物和鸟类的独特之处在于它们调节体温。”
“There’s no good evidence that any cold-blooded animal has REM sleep.”
“没有好的证据可以证明任何冷血动物都睡了REM。
REM sleep heats up the brain and non-REM cools it off, Siegel says, and that could mean that the changing sleep cycles allow the brain to repair itself.
Siegel说，REM睡眠会让大脑发热，而非REM会冷却它，这可能意味着睡眠周期的改变可以让大脑自我修复。
“It seems likely that REM sleep is filling a basic physiological function and that dreams are a kind of a side effect, or by-product of this.”
“似乎REM睡眠正在填补一种基本的生理功能，梦想是一种副作用，或者是它的副产品。”

paragraphs.brief: 人们对梦想的心理功能有很大的分歧，研究人员提出了一些不同的理论。
sentences: There is great disagreement about the psychological function of dreams and researchers have come up with some differing theories.
人们对梦想的心理功能有很大的分歧，研究人员提出了一些不同的理论。
On one side are scientists like Harvard’s Allan Hobson, who believes that dreams are essentially random.
一方面是哈佛的Allan Hobson这样的科学家，他们认为梦想基本上是随机的。

In the 1970s, Hobson and his colleague Robert McCarley proposed what they called the “activation-synthesis hypothesis,” which describes how dreams are formed by nerve signals sent out during REM sleep from a small area at the base of the brain called the pons.
20世纪70年代，霍布森和他的同事罗伯特·麦卡利提出了他们所谓的“活性合成假设 ” ( activation-synthesisis security)，描述梦想是如何由REM睡觉时从大脑底部一个叫“庞斯”的小区域发出的神经信号形成的。
These signals, the researchers said, activate the images that we call dreams.
研究人员说，这些信号激活了我们称之为梦想的图像。
That raised questions about dream research.
这引起了关于梦想研究的问题。
If dreams are insignificant night-time images created by the brain, what is the point of studying them?
如果梦是大脑创造的微不足道的夜空图像那么研究它们有什么意义呢？

paragraphs.brief: 科学家们利用PET和FMRI技术观察梦幻大脑发现REM最活跃的领域之一是控制我们情绪的边缘系统
sentences: But more recently, new theories have made some scientists take dreams more seriously.
但最近，新的理论使一些科学家更认真地对待梦想。
In 1997, Mark Solms of the University of Cape Town in South Africa found that there was more than one mechanism in the brain for activating dreams.
1997年，南非开普敦大学的Mark Solms发现，大脑中有一种以上的机制来激活梦想。

Since then, Solms has argued that medical diagnostic equipment like functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and positron emission tomography (PET) that helps researchers watch dreaming brains might actually lend new support to Freud’s ideas because the parts of the brain that are most active during dreaming control emotion.
自此以后，索姆斯认为，功能性磁共振成像(fMRI)和正方射线断层摄影(PET)等医疗诊断设备帮助研究人员观看梦想中的大脑，实际上可以给弗洛伊德的想法提供新的支持，因为大脑中最活跃的部分在梦想控制情感时。
Further research has supported Solms’s findings.
进一步的研究支持了索尔姆斯的调查结果。
Scientists using PET and fMRI technology to watch the dreaming brain have found that one of the most active areas during REM is the limbic system, which controls our emotions.
科学家们利用PET和FMRI技术观察梦幻大脑发现REM最活跃的领域之一是控制我们情绪的边缘系统

paragraphs.brief: 在REM睡眠期间，前额皮层的活性要小得多，因为它与逻辑思维有关。
sentences: Much less active during REM sleep is the prefrontal cortex, which is associated with logical thinking.
在REM睡眠期间，前额皮层的活性要小得多，因为它与逻辑思维有关。
That could explain why dreams in REM sleep often lack a coherent story line.
这可以解释为什么REM睡眠中的梦想往往缺乏一个连贯的故事线。
Some researchers have also found that people dream in non-REM sleep as well, although those dreams generally are less vivid.
一些研究人员还发现，人们也梦想在非REM睡眠中，尽管这些梦想一般不那么生动。
Another active part of the brain in REM sleep is the anterior cingulate cortex, which detects differences or inconsistencies.
REM睡眠中大脑的另一个活性部分是前额的螺旋皮层，它能检测出差异或不一致之处。
Eric Nofzinger, director of the Sleep Neuroimaging Program at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, thinks that could be why people often solve tricky problems in their dreams.
匹兹堡大学医疗中心睡眠神经成像计划主任Eric Nofzinger认为，这可能是人们常常在梦中解决棘手问题的原因。

paragraphs.brief: 有些研究者发现，梦想体力活，像体操运动员的地板常规一样，能提高性能。
sentences: Deirdre Barrett, assistant professor at Harvard Medical School, would agree.
Deirdre Barrett，哈佛医学院的助理教授，会同意的
In her book “The Committee of Sleep,” she describes how painters like Jasper Johns and Salvador Dali found inspiration in their dreams.
她的书《睡眠委员会》描述了贾斯珀·约翰斯和萨尔瓦多·达利等画家如何在他们的梦想中找到灵感。

In her own research on problem solving through dreams, Barrett has found that even ordinary people can solve simple problems in their lives (like how to fit old furniture into a new apartment) if they focus on the dilemma before they fall asleep.
巴雷特在她自己的关于通过梦想解决问题的研究中发现，即使普通人在睡着前也能够解决他们生活中的简单问题(比如如何把旧家具装进新公寓)。
There is also evidence that dreaming helps certain kinds of learning.
还有证据表明，梦想有助于某些类型的学习。
Some researchers have found that dreaming about physical tasks, like a gymnast’s floor routine, enhances performance.
有些研究者发现，梦想体力活，像体操运动员的地板常规一样，能提高性能。

paragraphs.brief: 马里兰大学的克拉拉山研究如何利用梦想进行治疗说梦是病人思考的“后门”
sentences: Whatever the function of dreams at night, they clearly can play a role in therapy during the day.
不管晚上做梦的功能如何白天做心理治疗时很明显他们可以扮演一个角色
The University of Maryland’s Clara Hill, who has studied the use of dreams in therapy, says that dreams are a “back door” into a patient’s thinking.
马里兰大学的克拉拉山研究如何利用梦想进行治疗说梦是病人思考的“后门”
“Dreams reveal stuff about you that you didn’t know was there,” she says.
”她说：「梦想揭露了你不知道的东西。
The therapists she trains to work with patients’ dreams use dream imagery to uncover hidden emotions and feelings.
她训练的治疗师们利用梦幻形象来揭开隐藏的情感和感情

Rosalind Cartwright from the university medical center in Chicago has been studying depression in divorced men and women, and she is finding that “good dreamers,” people who have vivid dreams with strong story lines, are less likely to remain depressed.
芝加哥大学医疗中心的罗莎琳德·卡特赖特一直在研究离婚男女的抑郁症，她发现“好梦想家”那些有着强烈故事线的生动梦想的人不太可能继续抑郁。
She thinks that dreaming helps diffuse powerful emotions.
她认为做梦有助于传播强大的情感
“Dreaming is a mental-health activity,” she says.
她说，“梦想是一种心理健康活动”。

items.en: a reference to the significance of dreams on artists’ work
items.zh: 提到梦想对艺术家工作的意义
items.why: F 段列举贾斯珀·约翰斯和萨尔瓦多·达利等画家从梦中得到灵感的例子，说明梦如何参与艺术创作。

items.en: a concern about the usefulness of dream research
items.zh: 对梦境研究的效用的关注
items.why: C 段提出反问：如果梦只是大脑夜间产生的无意义画面，研究它又有什么用？这反映了对梦研究价值的质疑。

items.en: the types of living creatures that have REM sleep
items.why: B 段指出，快速眼动睡眠普遍见于哺乳动物，甚至鸟类也有；随后又说明目前缺乏冷血动物经历此阶段的可靠证据。

items.en: research results linking dreams to psychological well-being
items.zh: 研究结果将梦想与心理健康联系起来
items.why: G 段描述对离婚人群的研究：经常做鲜明而有情节的梦的人，较不容易持续陷在抑郁中。这是梦与心理状态相关的研究发现。

items.en: an account of how modern research tools have strengthened Freud’s theory
items.zh: 描述现代研究工具如何强化了弗洛伊德的理论
items.why: D 段说明研究人员可以用功能性磁共振、正电子成像等设备观察做梦时的脑活动，并讨论这些发现怎样为弗洛伊德的解释提供支持。

According to the passage, which of the following happens during REM sleep?
items.zh: 根据这段路段，在REM睡觉时，会发生下列哪些情况？
correct: The temperature of the brain increases.

items.en: What explanation is suggested in paragraph E for lack of a clear narrative in dreams?
items.zh: E段建议如何解释，因为梦中缺乏明确的叙述？
correct: The part of the brain in control of reasoning is less involved.
大脑控制推理的部分参与较少。

items.en: According to the passage, which area of the brain helps people find solutions to difficult situations through their dreams?
items.zh: 大脑的哪个部分能帮助人们通过梦想找到解决困境的办法？

items.en: Technology shows there is a link between dreams and the areas of the brain that deal with feelings.
items.zh: 科技显示，梦想和大脑中处理感情的领域之间有联系。

items.en: Dreams are meaningless pictures created by the brain.
items.zh: 梦想是大脑创造的毫无意义的图片。
items.answer: B · Allan Hobson and Robert McCarley
items.solution: 艾伦·霍布森和罗伯特·麦卡利

items.en: Dreaming is a method of calming strong feelings.
items.zh: 做梦是平息强烈情绪的方法

items.en: Our dreams can show us unexpected things about ourselves.
items.zh: 我们的梦想能让我们看到自己出乎意料的事情

items.en: Dreams may be a result of maintaining an essential body function.
items.zh: 梦想可能是保持基本身体功能的结果。

points: C 段提出反问：如果梦只是大脑夜间产生的无意义画面，研究它又有什么用？这反映了对梦研究价值的质疑。
题干问“做梦是平息强烈情绪的方法”。定位句写到“芝加哥大学医疗中心的罗莎琳德·卡特赖特一直在研究离婚男女的抑郁症，她发现“好梦想家”那些有着强烈故事线的生动梦想的人不太可能继续抑郁”。
clauses: The mystery of REM sleep is that …, it is universal – at least in mammals and even birds.
连接词 though 引出“even though it may not be essential”，说明主句的让步关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 though 把这一层关系补进去。
REM sleep heats up the brain and non-REM cools it off, Siegel says, and that could mean ….
“that the changing sleep cycles allow the brain to repair itself”补足 mean 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 mean 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
lead: Dreams have captivated thinkers since ancient times, but their mystery is now closer than ever to resolution, thanks to new technology that allows scientists to watch the sleeping brain at work.
梦想自古以来就吸引了思想家，但其神秘感现在比任何时候都更接近于解答，感谢新技术让科学家们能够观察睡眠大脑的工作。
